issues.description: Pacing/real-time framing claim not delivered — only chunking is done
issues.detail: The PR description and changelog promise 'real-time pacing' for endpoints like Vonage Audio Connector, but the diff only slices bytes into fixed-size chunks and shoves them out as fast as the buffer fills. There is no sleep, no scheduler using _send_interval/_next_send_time for the packetized path, no clock. Vonage will get blasted with 100 packets in 50ms and then nothing. Either implement actual pacing (use the existing _next_send_time machinery you already have on the class) or stop claiming to do it in the docstring and changelog.

issues.description: Packet size in bytes with zero validation — silent misalignment on PCM16
issues.detail: fixed_audio_packet_size is a raw int with no constraint that it be even, let alone aligned to a sample frame (2 bytes for PCM16 mono, 4 for stereo). If someone passes 641, you will happily slice in the middle of a sample and emit garbage forever, with the remainder permanently misaligned because no resync logic exists. Either validate at setup (must be > 0 and multiple of bytes-per-sample-frame), or accept a duration in ms and compute bytes from sample_rate/channels/width. The current API hands users a footgun.

issues.description: InterruptionFrame ordering bug — buffer cleared after super(), buffer never flushed on stop
issues.detail: On InterruptionFrame the code clears _audio_send_buffer, fine. But there is no symmetric flush/drain anywhere — on EndFrame, disconnect, or when the buffer holds a sub-packet remainder forever after the last audio frame, that tail just sits there. Worse, the comment says 'drop partially buffered audio to avoid replaying stale PCM' but partial remainders also persist across normal speech boundaries because nothing else ever clears or pads them. Decide: pad-with-silence on flush, or drop. Pick one and do it on stop/end too, not only on interrupt.

This is three changes: (1) add VonageFrameSerializer, (2) add fixed_audio_packet_size packetization to FastAPI transport, (3) rename audio_packet_bytes to fixed_audio_packet_size. The rename is called out in the changelog but does not appear in the diff at all — either it's a stale changelog entry (lying to users) or it's a rename of something not yet merged (then say so). Split this: serializer is one patch, transport packetization is another, rename is a third (or drop it). Reviewing them mixed makes it impossible to revert one cleanly.

issues.description: bytearray copies on every send — gratuitously slow on the hot path
issues.detail: `self._audio_send_buffer.extend(bytes(payload))` converts payload to bytes (copy), then extends the bytearray (copy). Then `bytes(self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes])` slices (copy) then converts (copy). Then `del self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes]` shifts the tail (copy). That's 4-5 copies per packet on an audio fast path that runs every 20ms. Use a collections.deque of bytes chunks plus an index, or memoryview slicing. This is the kind of code that looks fine in review and tanks p99 latency in production.

issues.description: Non-audio payloads bypass the buffer and overtake buffered audio
issues.detail: The `return` after the buffered-send branch is correct for audio bytes, but consider the interleaving: if a JSON control message (e.g. a serialized OutputTransportMessageFrame) is emitted while audio sits in _audio_send_buffer, the JSON is sent immediately while the audio tail waits for more bytes. Order is silently reshuffled across modalities. At minimum document this; better, flush the audio buffer (padded or dropped per the policy you pick above) before emitting a non-audio payload.

issues.description: Copyright header says 2024-2025 in a 2026 commit
issues.detail: New file says 'Copyright (c) 2024–2025, Daily' but this is being added in 2026. Match the project's actual convention for new files; if other new files in this repo use the current year, fix it. Not blocking, but it's the kind of thing that suggests the file was copy-pasted from a template without thought.

issues.description: DTMF parsing tries two schemas with no source citation
issues.detail: `digit = message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit')` — the comment says 'Vonage may send digit in different formats, try both'. If the Vonage protocol actually has two formats, cite which versions or contexts produce which, in the docstring or a comment. Otherwise this reads as defensive programming against a spec the author didn't actually read. Pick the documented format; if both truly exist, name them.

Adds a new serializer and a new transport code path. Zero tests. The packetization buffer logic in particular (remainder handling, interruption clear, alignment) is exactly the kind of code that should have a unit test — it's pure, deterministic, and trivial to test without a websocket. Patches that add stateful buffering without tests will land bugs that bisect to this commit.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The Vonage serializer itself is mostly fine — small, readable, matches the existing serializer style. The transport-side packetization is where the patch falls down: it claims 'real-time pacing' but only does chunking with no actual clock, the packet size is unvalidated bytes (footgun on PCM alignment), the buffer is only cleared on interrupt and never flushed on end, and the hot path does 4-5 copies per packet. Also THREE-PATCHES: serializer, packetization, and a rename are mashed into one PR, and the changelog references a rename that doesn't appear in the diff. Split the patch, fix the alignment/validation, implement pacing or stop advertising it, and add tests for the buffer state machine.
